intro.text:
A wing section (NACA 0012) tilted steeply at 15° to the oncoming air.

What happens when a wing tilts too far?

outro.text:
That shaking is stall buffet, the warning pilots feel just before a wing stalls.

OpenFOAM pimpleFoam · 2D laminar, Re = 10 000

captions.text: Air flows left to right at 1 m/s. Colours show where it spins.
A big vortex grows over the top of the wing. The lift peaks at 3.3 s.
At 15° the air cannot follow the curved upper surface. It breaks away: the wing has stalled.
From about 10 s, vortices peel off in a steady rhythm, a new pair every 1.7 s.
With every vortex the lift swings between 0.66 and 1.23, so the wing would shake.
